Determine the equation of the line shown above if its slope is $\frac{1}{2}.$
q-44286.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ We know that the slope is $m=\frac{1}{2},$ so we just need to work out $y$-intercept $b.$

From the graph, we see that the line passes through the point $(2,4).$ Substituting this into $y=mx+b$ with $m=\frac{1}{2}$ and solving for $b,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\frac{1}{2}x+b \\ 4 & =\frac{1}{2}(2)+b \\ 4 & =1+b \\ b & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is $y=\frac{1}{2}x+3.$

The line shown above passes through the points $(0,-1)$ and $(1,2).$ What is the equation of the line?
q-22608.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

From the graph, we see that the line intercepts the $y$-axis at $(0,-1).$ So, the $y$-intercept is $b=-1.$

We can calculate the slope of the line by choosing two points on the line and applying the slope formula. The line passes through the points $(0,-1)$ and $(1,2),$ so we calculate its slope as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{2-(-1)}{1-0} \\  & =\frac{3}{1} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the slope $m=3$ and the $y$-intercept $b=-1$ into the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b,$ we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
y=3x-1

Substituting the slope m=3 and the y-intercept b=−1 into the slope-intercept form y=mx+b, we obtain the equation of the line:

y=3x−1

We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So, we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

From the graph, we see that the line intercepts the $y$-axis at $(0,-2).$ So, the $y$-intercept is $b=-2.$

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{1-(-2)}{4-0} \\  & =\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the slope $m=\frac{3}{4}$ and the $y$-intercept $b=-2$ into the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b,$ we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
y=\frac{3}{4}x-2
$$

q-6950.problem: Find the equation of the line that passes through the points $(4,1)$ and $(0,9).$
q-6950.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So, we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

First, we calculate the slope $m$ using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{9-1}{0-4} \\  & =\frac{8}{-4} \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

The coordinates of the $y$-intercept are always $(0,b).$ We know that the line passes through the point $(0,9),$ so the $y$-intercept is $b=9.$

Substituting the slope $m=-2$ and the $y$-intercept $b=9$ into the slope-intercept formula $y=mx+b,$ we reach

$$
y=-2x+9.
$$
